newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks hold losses ahead of Fed rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks hold losses ahead of Fed rate decision.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell Tuesday as investors grew anxious that the Federal Reserve's policy-makers might raise interest rates.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 45.75 points at 7,183.13.
In the broader market, declining issues beat advances by a 2-1 margin on volume of 206 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Bonds were also lower, with the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond off 9/32, which raised its yield to 6.94 percent from 6.92 percent at Monday's close. Prices and yields move in opposite directions.
"The market is having more sobering thoughts about what the Federal Reserve will do," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker.
Bill Allyn, head of trading at Jeffries & Co. said, "It's not panic selling; just a little pressure."
The Federal Open Market Committee, the central bank's policy-making arm, began meeting at 9 a.m. EDT 1300 GMT and was expected to announce a decision on interest rates around 2:15 p.m. EDT 1815 GMT.

At its last meeting in March, the inflation-wary Fed raised the key fed funds rate -- the rate commercial banks charge each other for overnight loans -- by one quarter percentage point. It was the first increase in more than two years.

Recent data has shown that inflation is not a threat. The Producer Price Index tumbled 0.6 percent in April, its biggest drop in nearly four years, while the Consumer Price Index rose just 0.1 percent.

Economists are split nearly down the middle on the outcome of the Fed's deliberations, with a slight majority forecasting no change in monetary policy, according to a Reuters survey released on Monday.
"It's too close to call, so now people are planning for after the Fed decision, no matter what happens," Cripps said.
If the Fed left the fed funds rate stand, the stock market could rally, perhaps strongly.
"If there's no (Fed) action, we could see a 40 or 50 point rally," one trader said.
But analysts found it tougher to forecast market response to a rate increase, with some expecting a sell-off but others convinced that stocks would take it in stride or maybe rise.

"The Fed's March rate increase took stocks lower but this one could see stocks rise because it could already be factored into markets," Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co said. "Either way, markets will be relieved."
Pierre Ellis, managing director at Primark Decision Economics, said the array of possible moves the Fed could make spooked markets.

"There are so many things the Fed could do," he said. "The action is that they will raise or not raise rates. But they could issue a statement on whether they think inflation is benign or threatening, which could affect markets."
Among individual stocks, Intel Corp. climbed 4 to 158-3/4, after Merrill Lynch said it expected the chipmaker's revenue growth to accelerate because of new products.
Electronic Data System Corp. was off 1-7/8 at 36. After the market close Monday, the company said it expected to report lower second quarter earnings.
The Nasdaq Composite index edged up 6.07 points to 1,347.31. The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks was off 3.89 points at 829.38.
